messages:
maya: heads-up — production pod p-42 (eu-west-1) saw 3 OOM kills in the last 10m after the kernel-selector tweak. impact: degraded tail latency + failed requests. kicking off triage here.

deploy-bot: [deploy] kernel-selector v2.17 -> v2.18 applied to autoscale-group 'inference-eu'. rollout: 100% (2026-03-17T09:12:03Z) :rocket:

li: logs show repeated failures allocating workspace for forward pass. stack: alloc_workspace -> attempted 192MB but only 64MB free. pattern looks like workspace sizing + fragmentation.

sam: quick mitigations we can try right now: 1) enable allocator soft-reserve (so small bursts don't trigger hard OOM) 2) reduce per-request workspace cap for big-seq requests (eg cap at 80MB) 3) activate circuit breaker to reject or reroute requests with >512 tokens to a cheaper variant.

jordan: i'm drafting a runtime patch to enable buffer reuse and lower default workspace. small PR to toggle reuse_cache and workspace_limit. snippet: ```yaml
runtime:
  allocator:
    reuse_cache_mb: 32
    soft_reserve_mb: 48
  workspace:
    default_limit_mb: 64
    large_request_limit_mb: 128
```

li: +1 to reuse_cache. also suggest enabling eviction-window: when total free < soft_reserve, evict LRU cached KV pages for that model. cheap win.

maya: plan for immediate actions (10m):
- roll back kernel-selector to v2.17 (if safe) OR apply allocator soft-reserve toggle (less risky)
- apply request-shaping policy to route >512-token requests to fallback model (embed-small)
- flip buffer_reuse cache=32MB on the affected pool
I'll execute the routing change, @jordan can you push the runtime toggle as a hotfix?

oncall-bot: @oncall-escalation paged: eng-runtime oncall (maya) — 3 OOMs detected on inference-eu pool.

sam: routing command ready: ```bash
# route policy: reject large or route to variant
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/policies \
  -d '{"name":"oom-protect-eu","match":{"model":"gpt-like-large","max_tokens":512},"action":{"route_to":"gpt-like-medium","mode":"route"}}'
```

jordan: hotfix PR opened: runtime: enable reuse_cache + soft_reserve default. diff (condensed): ```diff
+ allocator.reuse_cache_mb = 32
+ allocator.soft_reserve_mb = 48
- workspace.default_limit_mb = 96
+ workspace.default_limit_mb = 64
``` CI runs quick smoke. request to hotpatch to the affected pool only.

li: also enabling a temporary circuit-breaker at the LB: drop requests that would exceed queue_wait > 500ms for this pool. reduces compounding memory pressure.

maya: executing routing change now, rolling without downtime (traffic steering). jordan, after you hotpatch, please post the rollout status. I'll watch OOM counts + tail latency.

jordan: hotpatch deployed to inference-eu pool (canary 25% -> 100% within 4m). smoke passed. patch set: reuse_cache=32, soft_reserve=48, workspace_default=64.

li: profiler snapshot after changes (summary): free_mem before=1200MB, after hotpatch=1360MB; per-request average workspace reduced from 110MB -> 72MB; OOMs 3 -> 0 in last 8m. good signal.

sam: note for postmortem: kernel-selector change likely increased working set for some code-paths (different kernel chose larger temporary tensors). match profiling traces to kernel_choice histogram.

oncall-bot: incident annotation added: "mitigated by allocator soft-reserve + buffer reuse + request shaping".

maya: thanks everyone. next steps: 1) revert kernel-selector change until we understand root cause OR add a fallback in selector to prefer lower-workspace kernels for long sequences; 2) formalize an OOM mitigation runbook entry: include soft-reserve toggle, reuse_cache param, LB circuit-breaker thresholds, and routing snippet; 3) schedule an offline perf deep-dive (kernel histograms + trace).

jordan: I'll open follow-up issues: perf/regression-kernel-selector, runbooks/oom-mitigation-guidelines, runtime/allocator-tests. linking profiler dumps and allocator metrics.

maya: I'll draft a short incident note for all-hands and flag the Dedicated customers potentially affected. closing thread after we validate no regressions in 24h. :white_check_mark:
